issue.title: gateway: a GLM Coding Plan's key out of its window is read as a rate limit through the Anthropic endpoint, so a window reset by hand never lifts its rest
issue.body:
## What happens

A key on a GLM Coding Plan (Zhipu's or Z.ai's coding endpoint) that has spent its 5-hour, weekly or monthly window is refused 429. Through the **Anthropic** endpoint Zhipu types that 429 `rate_limit_error`, and its message names the window and when it is back:

```
Zhipu GLM: [1310][您已达到每周/每月使用上限，您的限额将在 2026-10-24 20:44:45 重置。][20261020091843ac61fce173a347a5]
```

`failure()` read the envelope's `rate_limit_error` as `rateWords` before `usedUpWords` (上限) was reached, so it said **rate**. `rateRest` then believed the reset the refusal named (#1669), resting the key until then — days off — and `renewed` lifts only quota/`window` rests, so a window its owner reset by hand never lifted it. Every request fell back to another provider for the days the window had left. Observed rest on 2026-10-20:

```
"rest":{"why":"rate","status":429,"until":"2026-10-24T20:44:45+08:00","by":"resets","failures":1,"key":"zhipu"}
```

Through the **Chat** endpoint the same refusal is untyped, reaches `usedUpWords` (上限), and is already `failQuota` — which is what #1024 built the plan's key around (rests to its window, read again as it is planned, lifted when a reading finds it renewed). This is that path, missed on the Anthropic endpoint.

## Fix

`failure()` reads the same words as out of quota (`zhipuResets`, the regex `resetsZhipu` already reads the reset time with), so the plan's key takes #1024's path whichever endpoint refused it. Zhipu's per-minute refusal (1302 请求太频繁) names no window and keeps its backoff, as #1024 holds.

## Test

`internal/gateway/glm_plan_quota_test.go` — `TestGLMPlanWindowSpentIsQuota`. Without the change:

```
--- FAIL: TestGLMPlanWindowSpentIsQuota (0.00s)
    glm_plan_quota_test.go:27: the Anthropic endpoint's refusal read as rate, want quota
```

With the change it passes, and holds the rest to `quota` by `resets` on the key's window id (`provider.KeyAllowanceID`), that planning reads the key's windows again (`restingOf`), and that `renewed` lifts it; the per-minute 1302 stays `rate`, and the words escaped as `\uXXXX` read the same (#1669).

## Patch

I could not open a PR from my account (GitHub refuses `CreatePullRequest` for it), so the patch is on a branch of my fork:

https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...ianfksyd:magpie:fix/glm-plan-quota-anthropic

It touches `internal/gateway/routing.go` (`failure()`), `internal/gateway/glm_plan_quota_test.go` (new) and `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`.

## What was run (at head `902ead2`)

- `gofmt -l internal/gateway/routing.go internal/gateway/glm_plan_quota_test.go` — nothing printed
- `go vet ./...` — no issues
- `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` — no issues
- `go build ./...`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go build ./...` — ok
- `go test ./internal/gateway/ -count=1` — passed
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -count=1` — passed
- `go test -tags nogui ./...` — passed, 11499 tests in 85 packages

Not run: the GUI suite (no GUI change).

comments.body:
A GLM Coding Plan key out of its window was read as rate through the Anthropic endpoint because `failure()` matched `rateWords` before the quota words, so the key rested until the named reset and `renewed` never lifted it.

The branch reads `zhipuResets` and `usedUpWords` as quota before `rateWords`, so the plan key takes the quota path on both the Anthropic and OpenAI-shaped endpoints; the per-minute 1302 refusal stays rate.

[fix/3013-glm-window-quota](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3013-glm-window-quota), commit b1ab1dad53ec1f7bd2015581e9cf8ebb762a7372.

Ran `TestGLMPlanWindowSpentIsQuota` (failed before the change, passes after), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/gateway/`, and the `internal/gateway` package suite.

Fork branch, ready to review.

Still reproducible on **v0.1.3533** (macOS, 2026-11-10), through the Anthropic endpoint with `zcode/GLM-5.3` (GLM Coding Pro, zcode plugin).

Upstream 429, verbatim:

```
[1308][已达到 5 小时的使用上限。您的限额将在 2026-11-10 16:01:04 重置。][202611101433583360720d4c25418e]
```

Every request through magpie replayed the same body plus the core's suffix:

```
(rate limited: not asked again before 16:01 UTC+8)
```

After the 5-hour window was reset by hand on the ZCode side, `magpie quota` already reported the new window (`5h 26% ↻4h20m 19:38`, and `↺ 5 five-hour resets until Nov 23 21:06`) — the upstream was serving again — but the rest still pointed at the old `16:01:04`.

`magpie daemon restart` does not clear it by itself: the first request after the restart still replayed the old 429, and the next one returned HTTP 200 (2.0s, 13in / 16out).

Checked main as of 2026-11-10: `plannedWords` still does not contain 「小时的使用上限」, and `failure()` has no branch that reads `zhipuResets` / `usedUpWords` before `rateWords`, so an Anthropic-shaped 1308 is still classified as `rate` and `renewed()` can never lift it. This is the same diagnosis you gave, just later code.

Your `fix/3013-glm-window-quota` branch (`b1ab1dad`) addresses exactly this path. I don't see a PR against yetone/magpie referencing this issue, so it looks like the fix is still only on the fork.

One more data point for the same report: `magpie quota reset` only covers Codex accounts, so there is no CLI way to lift a ZCode rest — the only user-side workaround is to get one request through successfully, or wait for the named time.

## Result

I independently replayed @skygunner's `b1ab1dad53ec1f7bd2015581e9cf8ebb762a7372` on `origin/main@401187300`. The regression is still present at the clean tip, and the reported classification path turns green on a minimal current-tip adaptation.

## Evidence

- With only the author's `TestGLMPlanWindowSpentIsQuota` copied onto clean `401187300`, the Anthropic-shaped 1310 refusal is still classified as `rate` rather than `quota`.
- The original commit does not apply cleanly to the current tip: the conflict is the later `minuteLimit` → `minuteRate` change. Keeping current `minuteRate` and placing the author's `zhipuResets` check before it resolves the conflict without changing the diagnosis.
- The replayed test, other GLM plan tests, and nearby Zhipu tests pass with `-count=5`.
- The test covers the Anthropic-shaped and OpenAI-shaped spent-window bodies, while the per-minute 1302 refusal remains `rate`.
- `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Windows full-repo `go vet ./...` / `go build ./...`, and `internal/gateway` Windows/Linux vet/build pass.

## Boundary

This is independent verification of @skygunner's existing branch, not a competing patch. On the current tip, the only necessary delta appears to be the Zhipu reset check before `minuteRate`; the original commit should not be treated as a clean cherry-pick.

## Gap / Not tried

- I did not request a real exhausted Zhipu/Z.ai plan key.
- I did not run the full `internal/gateway` test suite in this review pass.
- The exact 1308 body added by @wf2311 was confirmed by their live reproduction, but I did not send it to a real plan key.

## Action

@skygunner's branch remains the candidate to rebase against the current tip. Please keep the reset-window handling and the 1302 rate-limit case in the final test matrix.

issue.title: gateway: a LiteLLM "Budget has been exceeded" 429 reads as a short rate limit, so quota-rest until HH:MM never applies

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

A custom OpenAI-compatible relay backed by **LiteLLM** refuses a request with a 429 whose body says the key's budget is spent:

```
429 · Budget has been exceeded! Key=… (sk-…), Current cost: <spent>, Max budget: <cap>
```

`failure()` does not read this as *used up*: the word list has `budget (exceeded|exhausted)` and `out of budget`, but "Budget **has been** exceeded" has "has been" between the two words, and no `quota` / `insufficient` / `billing` word appears, so the refusal falls through to the short-rate-limit branch. The key then rests 1 minute, doubled each time, capped at 30 minutes:

```
"rest":{"why":"rate","status":429,"until":"2026-11-04T00:31:08.872929984+08:00","by":"backoff","failures":7,"key":"my-relay","error":"my-relay: Budget has been exceeded! Key=… Current cost: <spent>, Max budget: <cap>"}
```

That cap is the point of the report: a budget that is spent does not come back in 30 minutes, so the key is probed again (a free, token-less 429) every ≤30 minutes until its budget resets. I had configured `magpie provider quota-rest <id> '08:00'` for exactly this daily-reset budget, but it never applies because the refusal never reaches the used-up branch — the documented "first of these that is known" ladder in `docs/reference.md` ("When an account runs out") skips straight to the rate-limit branch.

This is the same shape as #3013 (a quota refusal read as `rate` because of envelope/wording), just on the wording side instead of the endpoint side.

## Expected

A 429 whose body says the key's budget/allowance is spent is classified out-of-quota (`failQuota`), so:

- `magpie provider quota-rest <id> '08:00'` (or any duration) governs the rest, per `docs/reference.md`;
- the rest is lifted by a reading that finds the budget back (like window rests), not only by the rest expiring.

## Suggested fix

Widen the used-up word list in `internal/gateway/routing.go` (`failure()`) to read "budget" and "exceeded" (or "has been exceeded") in any order within the sentence, e.g. a pair-check `budget` + `exceed|exhaust` rather than the adjacent bigram. LiteLLM's sentence begins `Budget has been exceeded!` and mentions the budget again later in the same body ("Max budget: …"), so even a loose "contains `budget`" check would catch it.

The relay's per-minute rate limit (`LiteLLM: Rate limit exceeded` style) names no budget and should keep its `rate` backoff.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.2811, gateway on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
- provider: custom relay, OpenAI-compatible `/v1`, LiteLLM behind it
- model group routing `weight`, one key per provider

Happy to test a build or provide more of the routing log if useful.
